Contracts Beyond Drawing

Source: vignettes/contracts-beyond-shapes.Rmd
contracts-beyond-shapes.Rmd
library(S7)
library(s7contract)

The introductory examples for s7contract use drawable shapes because the methods are easy to see. The same machinery can describe less visual contracts: “number-like” objects, “vector-like” objects, adapters around storage classes, or small protocol boundaries between packages.

These examples are intentionally modest. s7contract checks runtime S7 methods; it does not turn R into a statically typed language.

A small Number-ish interface

A full mathematical Number abstraction is too ambitious for this package: arithmetic is often binary or multi-dispatch, base vectors have recycling rules, and numerical code usually needs performance more than abstraction. A small single-dispatch interface can still be useful when a function only needs a few operations.

num_zero <- new_generic("num_zero", "x")
num_add <- new_generic("num_add", "x")
num_scale <- new_generic("num_scale", "x")
num_value <- new_generic("num_value", "x")

NumberLike <- new_interface(
  "NumberLike",
  methods = list(
    zero = num_zero,
    add = num_add,
    scale = num_scale,
    value = num_value
  )
)

method(num_zero, class_double) <- function(x) 0
method(num_add, class_double) <- function(x, y) x + y
method(num_scale, class_double) <- function(x, k) x * k
method(num_value, class_double) <- function(x) x

implements(class_double, NumberLike)
#> [1] TRUE
num_add(10, 5)
#> [1] 15
num_scale(10, 0.5)
#> [1] 5

This is a protocol rather than a promise that every numeric law holds. If you need associativity, units, precision guarantees, missing-value rules, or multi-dispatch over both operands, those rules must be documented and tested separately.

The explicit trait layer can make the contract nominal. A class has the trait only after an impl_trait() call records it.

Numberish <- new_trait(
  "Numberish",
  methods = list(
    zero = trait_method(num_zero),
    add = trait_method(num_add),
    scale = trait_method(num_scale),
    value = trait_method(num_value)
  ),
  assoc_consts = list(FAMILY = "scalar")
)

impl_trait(
  Numberish,
  class_integer,
  methods = list(
    zero = function(x) 0L,
    add = function(x, y) x + y,
    scale = function(x, k) as.integer(x * k),
    value = function(x) x
  )
)

has_trait(2L, Numberish)
#> [1] TRUE
trait_call(Numberish, "add", 2L, 3L)
#> [1] 5
trait_assoc_const(Numberish, 2L, "FAMILY")
#> [1] "scalar"

A Vector-ish interface

A vector-like contract can be more practical. Many algorithms only need to know how long a thing is, how to slice it, and how to expose its values.

vec_length <- new_generic("vec_length", "x")
vec_slice <- new_generic("vec_slice", "x")
vec_values <- new_generic("vec_values", "x")

VectorLike <- new_interface(
  "VectorLike",
  methods = list(
    length = vec_length,
    slice = vec_slice,
    values = vec_values
  )
)

ReadDepth <- new_class(
  "ReadDepth",
  properties = list(
    position = class_integer,
    depth = class_double
  ),
  validator = function(self) {
    if (length(self@position) != length(self@depth)) {
      "@position and @depth must have the same length"
    }
  }
)

method(vec_length, ReadDepth) <- function(x) length(x@depth)
method(vec_slice, ReadDepth) <- function(x, i) {
  ReadDepth(position = x@position[i], depth = x@depth[i])
}
method(vec_values, ReadDepth) <- function(x) x@depth

method(vec_length, class_double) <- function(x) length(x)
method(vec_slice, class_double) <- function(x, i) x[i]
method(vec_values, class_double) <- function(x) x

coverage <- ReadDepth(
  position = 1:5,
  depth = c(12, 15, 9, 20, 17)
)

implements(coverage, VectorLike)
#> [1] TRUE
vec_length(coverage)
#> [1] 5
vec_values(vec_slice(coverage, 2:4))
#> [1] 15  9 20

A function can assert the small interface it needs and then call only those required operations.

window_mean <- function(x, i) {
  assert_implements(x, VectorLike)
  mean(vec_values(vec_slice(x, i)))
}

window_mean(coverage, 2:4)
#> [1] 14.66667
window_mean(c(12, 15, 9, 20, 17), 2:4)
#> [1] 14.66667

Bad ideas to reject early

Idea Why it sounds appealing Critique
A universal Number trait for all arithmetic One abstraction for integers, doubles, complex numbers, units, sparse arrays, and domain objects R arithmetic has recycling, missing values, attributes, and binary dispatch needs. Keep the contract narrow and test algebraic laws separately.
A Vector trait that replaces base vectors or vctrs One API for every sequence-like object Existing vector semantics are deep and battle-tested. Use a tiny protocol at package boundaries, not as a replacement for mature vector frameworks.
Traits as static type checks Compile-time confidence sounds nice Checks happen at runtime. They are useful assertions and documentation, not a compiler.
Interfaces for every helper function More contracts can look more rigorous Too many tiny contracts add ceremony. Define contracts only at boundaries where substitutability matters.

The productive pattern is to name a small behavior, state what it does not guarantee, and keep examples small enough to run during R CMD check.
